newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Toyota buys 27.8 pct stake in Toyota SA.
newsitem.headline: Toyota buys 27.8 pct stake in Toyota SA.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said on Tuesday it had bought a 27.8 percent stake in Toyota South Africa Ltd for 456 million rand from Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd (Johnnic).

Shinji Sakai, senior managing director of Toyota Motor Corp, told President Nelson Mandela who attended the announcement, that the purchase of the stake was in response to his request for investment from Japan.
"You, Mr President have requested that Japan invest in South Africa...It has now come about that we are acquire that shares of Toyota South Africa held by Johnnic," Sakai said.
Bert Wessels, chairman of Toyota SA, welcoming the investment said: "The investment is 456 million rand. It will help us accelerate our production technology to world standards."
Mandela said he was delighted that Toyota had responded so swiftly to his request for Japanese investment.
He added that arguments that the government was trying to develop black millionaires through black economic empowerment was not true.
"Blacks should move to companies whose ultimate aim is manufacturing so that they can provide jobs to the large numbers of people without jobs," Mandela said.
"One of Johnnic's aims is to move to providing jobs."
Vaughan Bray, chief executive of Johnnic said his company had heard Toyota Motor Corp was keen on investing in South Africa.
"We heard that Toyota Motor Corp was interested in making an investment in South Africa...We took a decision to sell the shares to them."
